title: Retroactive Withdrawal Request Spanning Pre-Merge Enrollment Terms
scenario_text:
**Email — Subject: "Retroactive withdrawal petition — Jordan Akiyama" (May 28, 2026)**
From: jordan.akiyama@brightpath.edu
To: registrar@brightpath.edu
CC: disabilityservices@brightpath.edu

Hi, I'm requesting a retroactive withdrawal from Spring 2024. I was hospitalized for most of that term (documentation attached) and received all F grades. I've since returned and am doing well, but those grades are destroying my GPA and affecting my eligibility for the teaching credential program. My disability services coordinator said this should be straightforward given the medical documentation.

**Banner SIS — Student Record (ID: BSU-2020-07734)**
Name: Jordan Akiyama | Admit: Fall 2020 (West campus, pre-merge) | Catalog: 2020-21
Spring 2024 enrollment: 15 credits (5 courses) | Grades: F, F, F, F, W
Cumulative GPA: 2.14 (would be 2.87 without Spring 2024 Fs)
Program: BA Education — Teaching Credential Track

**Banner — Academic Policy Configuration**
Retroactive Withdrawal Policy (effective Fall 2023, Policy #AR-2023-07):
"Petitions must be filed within 12 months of the affected term's end date. Requires documentation of extenuating circumstances. Approved by Associate Registrar."

**Slack — #registrar-ops (May 29, 2026, 11:15 AM)**
@sarah.p: Michael — the Akiyama retro-W petition just came in. It's for Spring 2024. That's past the 12-month window, right?
@michael.o: When did Spring 2024 end? May 2024. So the deadline was May 2025. Yeah, it's a year past.
@sarah.p: The student says disability services told them it would be fine.
@michael.o: Did they file an extension with us before the deadline?
@sarah.p: Doesn't look like it.
@michael.o: Check if they were under the old West campus policy though. The 12-month limit was new with AR-2023-07.

**SharePoint — Archived Policies (West Campus Legacy)**
File: WestPDX_AcademicRegulations_2020.pdf
Section 9.4 — Retroactive Withdrawal:
"Students may petition for retroactive withdrawal at any time prior to degree conferral. No time limit. Requires documentation of circumstances beyond the student's control and approval by the Academic Standards Committee."

**Google Sheet — "Academic Standards Committee Decisions 2024-25" (last row: Apr 2026)**
[No entry for Jordan Akiyama]
Column headers: Student ID | Term | Petition Type | Decision | Approved By | Notes
Row 112 (Mar 2025): BSU-2019-03341 | Fall 2023 | Retro-W | APPROVED | Committee | "Pre-merge student — applied West campus regs per transition memo"
Row 113 (Mar 2025): BSU-2021-08822 | Spring 2023 | Retro-W | DENIED | Committee | "Enrolled under unified policy — 12-month window applies"

**Google Doc — "Campus Merger Transition Memorandum" (authored by VP Academic Affairs, Jul 2021)**
Section 4.1: "Students admitted to West or East campuses prior to Fall 2021 retain the academic regulations of their admitting campus for the duration of continuous enrollment, unless the unified regulation is more favorable to the student."
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @assoc.provost, Aug 2023]: "Does this sunset? We can't maintain two policy sets forever."
[Reply in thread by @vp.acad]: "Operationally yes, but we never set a formal sunset. Legal says we're bound until we formally supersede with notice to affected students. Put it on the governance agenda."
[No further action visible in any system]
question: Is Jordan Akiyama eligible to petition for retroactive withdrawal from Spring 2024, and under which policy framework?

contributor.name: Michael Owusu
contributor.title: Associate Registrar
contributor.domain_expertise: Enrollment verification, transfer credit evaluation, academic policy interpretation, FERPA compliance, degree audit exceptions

choices: No — the petition is past the 12-month deadline under AR-2023-07, which is the current unified policy. The student should have filed by May 2025.

Yes — as a pre-merge West campus student with continuous enrollment, the West campus policy (no time limit) applies per the transition memorandum; however, the petition must go to the Academic Standards Committee, not the Associate Registrar.

No — while the West campus policy might technically apply, the Academic Standards Committee has not yet received the petition, and precedent shows the committee process takes months; the student should instead appeal the F grades individually through the grade appeal process.

Yes — the transition memorandum applies, and since AR-2023-07 doesn't have a time limit component that is 'more favorable,' the West policy governs entirely, meaning the Associate Registrar can approve it directly.
